fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly treated as a single-phase solid solution; the target is an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA containing FCC and B2 phases.
The proposed oxygen-complex intervention is unrelated to the target intervention, which is intermediate-temperature aging used to control L12 ordering and FCC/B2 phase-boundary evolution.
The hypothesis omits the central non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition, including minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The claimed link from short-range-order hardening to preserved toughness is not established; increased strength or ordering does not by itself imply improved toughness.
The cited evidence supports effects of interstitial oxygen or nitrogen on strength and ductility in other HEAs, but does not support toughness retention after the proposed 700°C exposure.
explanation: The response addresses thermal exposure, subsequent loading, a treated-versus-untreated comparison, and provides a nominally falsifiable mechanical test, so it has limited alignment with the requested hypothesis format. Scientifically, however, it does not reconstruct the target. It replaces thermal-aging control of L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries with ordered oxygen complexes, gives only a vague 700°C condition rather than the relevant <550°C, 550–750°C, and >750°C regimes, and predicts generic toughness improvement instead of a ductile-brittle-ductile response. Its experiment could test the proposed alternative, but it does not isolate oxygen-complex formation or test the target signatures of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips while excluding impurity segregation. The supporting citations establish, at most, that interstitial additions can alter HEA mechanical properties; they do not validate post-aging toughness preservation.
